content.title: Synthetic Paper Bridge Contract
content.summary: Compare paper shapes and improve a bridge so it supports more equal test pieces.
content.openingQuestion: Can one sheet of paper bridge a gap and hold a load?
content.adultBrief: Folds can make paper more resistant to bending.
content.adultDetail: Changing the cross-sectional shape changes how paper resists bending and distributes a load. Results depend on paper, span, folds, and load placement.
content.childExplanation: A flat sheet bends easily. Folds make little walls that help it keep its shape.
reflections: What stayed the same for a fair test?

learn.goal: Run two comparable tests and use the result to improve one paper shape.
learn.method: Changing only the paper shape makes bending resistance visible while equal loads provide evidence for comparison.

skills.name: Fold paper with control
evidence: Makes repeated folds with decreasing help.

skills.name: Count one test piece at a time
evidence: Adds one piece and updates the count once.

skills.name: Use test results to redesign
evidence: Names one change and retests it under equal conditions.

decisions: Choose one paper-shape change for the improvement test.
lookFors: Notice the amount of help used for each assigned action without grading predictions or physical results.

guidance.rationale: With no prior evidence, one-to-one counting during a real test is a useful starting opportunity for ages five to six.
guidance.simplify: Use fewer blocks and let the child touch each block while saying the number.
guidance.extend: Ask the child to recover the total after each waiting interval.

guidance.rationale: With no prior evidence, proposing, testing, and revising a personal design provides an open challenge for ages seven to eight.
guidance.simplify: Offer two approved shapes and ask the child to choose one and predict its behavior.
guidance.extend: Ask the child to justify the redesign with two observations.

guidance.rationale: Folding is available to every participant but is selected as a primary objective only when evidence makes it useful.
guidance.simplify: Mark guides or stabilize the sheet while the child completes the fold.
guidance.extend: Ask the child to plan and repeat a chosen fold interval.

materials.name: Equal copy-paper sheets
materials.safety: Stop if a paper cut occurs.

substitutes.name: Equal construction-paper sheets
substitutes.conditions: Run a new baseline with every bridge shape.

materials.name: Equal large test blocks
materials.prep: Choose pieces too large to swallow.
materials.safety: Never use coins, glass, or heavy weights.

states.text: Materials are prepared and no result is known.
Every child has observed the flat-sheet baseline.
Every child has selected a paper shape.
Every child has a labeled bridge ready to test.
Every child completed a test and has a result.
The group selected and tested one improvement.
Every child connected a design to an observation.
Materials are counted and safely stored.

materialFunctions.purpose: The paper is the bridge; its shape is the changed variable.
Each equal block is one load unit added during a test.

roles.name: Child investigator — folding focus
roles.contribution: Completes the full cycle while the adult observes folding support.
responsibilities: Propose, build, test, observe, recommend, and explain a personal bridge.

roles.name: Child investigator — counting focus
roles.contribution: Completes the full cycle while the adult observes one-to-one counting.
responsibilities: Propose, build, test, observe, recommend, and explain a personal bridge.

roles.name: Child investigator — redesign focus
roles.contribution: Completes the full cycle while the adult observes evidence-based redesign.
responsibilities: Propose, build, test, observe, recommend, and explain a personal bridge.

groups.notes: The child completes one full personal cycle.
Both children complete a personal cycle; focus changes only the observation cue.
Every child completes a personal cycle; the group shares one improvement.

steps.title: Ask
steps.purpose: Elicit a prediction before anyone knows the outcome.
steps.transition: The observed flat-sheet result creates a concrete problem to solve.
steps.instruction: Show the gap and ask what a paper bridge needs to do.

adultActions.text: Position the supports and show one unloaded flat sheet.

prompts.text: What do you think the paper will do when we add the test pieces?

participantActions.text: Point, say, or draw a prediction without needing to be correct.

materialUses.purpose: Create equal load units in the baseline test.

steps.decision: Choose whether to answer by pointing, speaking, or drawing.

cues.behavior: Offers a testable prediction or question.
cues.doNotInfer: Prediction accuracy is not evidence of understanding.

steps.result: Children identify the span and load.

problems.problem: A child seeks the correct prediction.
problems.safeResponse: Record every prediction without grading it.

steps.warning: Only the adult positions the supports.
steps.resume: Return to the same support spacing.

steps.title: Predict
steps.purpose: Turn several ideas into one testable shape and one fair condition.
steps.transition: The baseline observation gives every child evidence for choosing a shape.
steps.instruction: Draw or describe a paper shape that may resist bending.

adultActions.text: Show the flat sheet and the approved folded-shape diagram without naming a winner.

prompts.text: Without adding paper, what shape could we give this sheet? What must stay the same?

participantActions.text: Choose or draw a personal paper shape, predict its behavior, and name one condition that remains equal.

materialUses.purpose: Represent or demonstrate approved shape choices.

steps.decision: Every child chooses one approved shape for a personal test.

cues.behavior: Names one change and one condition to keep equal.
cues.doNotInfer: Choosing a suggested option alone is not independent redesign evidence.

steps.result: Each child can offer an idea.
steps.success: At least one shape is selected.

problems.safeResponse: Choose one change for each test.

steps.warning: Do not add a load during prediction.
steps.resume: Keep the selected drawing with the materials.

steps.title: Build one personal bridge per child
steps.purpose: Turn every selected idea into a testable one-sheet structure while preserving the flat reference.
steps.transition: Every selected idea becomes a labeled structure that can be tested.
steps.instruction: Give every child one equal sheet to build and label a personal bridge shape.

adultActions.text: Offer guides or stabilize the sheet without replacing the child's design decisions.

prompts.text: Show me the shape you chose and tell me when your bridge is ready to test.

participantActions.text: Build and label a personal bridge shape with available support.

materialUses.purpose: Give every child an equal sheet for a personal design.

cues.behavior: Continues the fold-turn sequence with the recorded amount of help.
cues.doNotInfer: Do not rate folding if the adult created the folds.

steps.result: Every child has a labeled bridge that can span the same gap one at a time.
steps.success: Every participant can identify a personal structure and its test orientation.

problems.safeResponse: Use stable supports or reduce the span.

steps.warning: Use intact paper and no sharp fasteners.
steps.resume: Keep every bridge beside its name or symbol and planned orientation.

steps.title: Give every child a personal test
steps.purpose: Produce one comparable result per child by adding and counting one equal load at a time.
steps.transition: Each personal structure is tested under the same conditions to produce a result.
steps.instruction: Reset the setup, then let each child test a personal bridge with one equal block at a time.

adultActions.text: Before each design, reset the supports, center the bridge, and give the ready signal.

prompts.text: One piece, one number, then wait. Tell me if anything besides the paper changes.

participantActions.text: In a personal turn, check the setup, add and count one equal piece at a time, observe the bridge, and keep the result.

materialUses.purpose: Serve as each child's bridge during a personal test.
Provide identical load units for every test.

cues.behavior: Uses one number for each piece and recovers the count after waiting.
cues.doNotInfer: A setup failure is not evidence about counting ability.

steps.result: Every child has a valid result or a documented non-comparable test.
steps.success: Every child tested a bridge using the same span, container, and load units.

problems.safeResponse: Stop, clear the load, and restart the test.

steps.warning: Keep faces away and stop if a support moves.
steps.resume: Record the last complete test before pausing.

steps.title: Choose one change
steps.purpose: Use the first comparison to choose and test one deliberate change.
steps.transition: Personal results support recommendations for one shared improvement.
steps.instruction: Change one feature and predict the effect.

adultActions.text: Show only approved shape options and keep paper, span, and load unchanged.

prompts.text: What did the first tests show? Which one change should we try next?

participantActions.text: Recommend one change using a personal result and help the group choose one.
Contribute to building and testing the selected group improvement.

materialUses.purpose: Build the shared improvement from the selected recommendation.
Retest the group design with the same load units.

steps.decision: Choose the single shape feature to change.

cues.behavior: Uses a prior result to select one new feature.
cues.doNotInfer: The redesigned bridge does not need to hold more for the decision to count.

steps.result: The group names one deliberate change.

problems.safeResponse: Keep one change and save the rest for another test.

steps.warning: Do not increase load weight or support height.
steps.resume: Mark the one feature selected for change.

steps.title: Explain with evidence
steps.purpose: Connect a claim about shape to something seen or counted.
steps.transition: Visible designs and results let every child explain a connection from their own experience.
steps.instruction: Compare counts and describe where each bridge bent.

adultActions.text: Place unloaded designs side by side and point to the recorded results.

prompts.text: What did you see or count that supports your idea?

participantActions.text: Share one observation by speaking, pointing, drawing, or choosing.

materialUses.purpose: Keep each personal and group design visible for explanation.
Refer to the recorded load counts without reloading the bridges.

steps.decision: Choose which observation or result to use in the explanation.

cues.behavior: Links one shape or change to a visible or counted result.
cues.doNotInfer: Repeating the adult explanation is not independent evidence.

steps.success: A shape is linked to a result.

problems.problem: The explanation does not cite a result.
problems.safeResponse: Point to the recorded counts or visible bending.

steps.resume: Keep the recorded counts with the bridges.

steps.title: Clean
steps.purpose: Close the practical cycle by accounting for materials and leaving a safe space.
steps.transition: The investigation is complete, so materials can be counted and safely stored.
steps.instruction: Count all blocks and store or recycle paper.

adultActions.text: Remove supports first and verify the floor and table before leaving.

prompts.text: Let us account for every piece and choose which paper to keep or recycle.

participantActions.text: Count, sort, and store materials after the adult removes supports.

materialUses.purpose: Choose which designs to keep or recycle.
Account for and store every test unit.

steps.decision: Choose which intact paper designs to keep or recycle.

cues.behavior: Accounts for one stored piece at a time with available support.
cues.doNotInfer: Cleanup participation is an exposure unless the adult chooses Evaluate more.

steps.result: The table and floor are clear.

problems.safeResponse: Keep the area closed until the adult finds it.

steps.warning: Account for every test piece before leaving.
steps.resume: Cleanup must finish before another activity.

safety.supervision: An adult remains present and controls material selection.

controls.text: Use only large blocks and account for each one.

stops.text: Stop if a child mouths a piece or a support becomes unstable.

prohibited.text: Do not use sharp, breakable, hot, or heavy loads.

adaptations.name: Short comparison
adaptations.conditions: Use when only 35 minutes are available.
adaptations.changes: Test flat and accordion shapes once.

closeout.question: How independently did the child make controlled folds?
How independently did the child add and count one block at a time?
How independently did the child use a test result to choose one redesign?
evidence: Named a result and changed one feature.
